item.title: Trump's U.N. envoy says Iran war could drag on for another year
item.description: The U.S. ambassador to the U.N. says the war with Iran could last another year, but he hopes Tehran will "come to the table" sooner.

item.title: Trump says new fuel supply push will lower prices. Will it work?
item.description: The Trump administration said using the DPA funding will increase refining output and lower fuel prices for Americans. Experts are skeptical.

item.title: What we know as Netanyahu vows major military operation in West Bank after deadly attack on troops
item.description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu says he's ordered a major military operation in the occupied West Bank after a shooting attack by two Palestinian men that killed two soldiers. CBS News' Dov Lieber and Robert Berger have more.

item.title: Police officer resigns after shooting that killed 1-year-old
item.description: The Mississippi attorney general's office had determined that the use of force was justified in the deadly shooting that stemmed from an alleged shoplifting incident.

item.title: PHP bug "about as bad as it can get," cybersecurity reporter says
item.description: A bug in the PHP programming language could put up to 70% of the world's websites at risk, experts say. Reuters cybersecurity reporter Raphael Satter explains more about this critical vulnerability.

item.title: A Florida cop found a dead man, had him cremated and stole his identity, prosecutors say
item.description: A Florida police officer is accused of stealing a dead man's identity and then moving into his home. CBS News Miami's Chelsea Jones has more.

item.title: AOC campaigns for Troy Jackson in Maine; Tafoya makes strides in Minnesota
item.description: New York progressive Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez is campaigning for Maine Democratic Senate candidate Troy Jackson. Meanwhile, the Senate race in typically blue Minnesota is tightening. CBS News' Taurean Small reports.

item.title: Trump doubles down on support for Ramaswamy ad
item.description: Ohio Republican gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy released a controversial attack ad featuring opponent Amy Acton's mother. President Trump repeatedly defended the ad, despite bipartisan backlash. CBS News' Weijia Jiang reports, plus Ed O'Keefe takes a look at other midterm elections to watch.

item.title: Trump defends Ramaswamy ad, takes questions on midterms, Iran war and more
item.description: President Trump spoke to reporters outside the White House before heading to a campaign stop in Florida.

item.title: AI agents accessing bank accounts without approval, report says
item.description: Some AI agents are accessing bank accounts without users' approval, according to Axios, raising questions about the safeguards in place to protect sensitive information.

item.title: Did High-Speed Rail help consultants "manipulate" a bid to win a lucrative contract?
item.description: Records show California High-Speed Rail knew a winning contract bid relied on "artificially low" rates that the consulting firm never intended to charge.

item.title: Buttigieg endorses independent Seth Bodnar in Montana Senate race
item.description: Pete Buttigieg chose to endorse independent Seth Bodnar over the Democratic Senate nominee, Alani Bankhead. Bodnar says he will not caucus with Democrats if he wins.

item.title: 2 ex-FBI officials charged with lying about Hunter Biden laptop probe
item.description: Two former FBI agents have each been charged with one count of lying to Congress about the investigation into Hunter Biden's laptop.

item.title: House hunter discovers deceased body in vacant home
item.description: In an exclusive interview, a homebuyer shares vivid details of finding a dead man during a house tour.

item.title: Trump administration to push for new labels on seafood
item.description: The Trump administration intends to push for new labels on seafood sold at grocery stores to give consumers a better idea of where products originated.

item.title: Meghan Markle reacts to "disturbing" child sex abuse accusations against estranged father
item.description: For years, Meghan Markle, the Duchess of Sussex, has had a strained relationship with her estranged father Thomas Markle. He did not attend her 2018 wedding to Prince Harry. Now, Markle is publicly sharing her distress after allegations her father possessed images of child sexual abuse.

item.title: DOJ sues to block Alaska Senate certification if Sullivan loses
item.description: The Justice Department is asking the federal court to block certification if Sen. Sullivan loses, but would have won had the other Sullivan's votes been counted for him.

item.title: "Subway Takes" star Debbie Shields "never thought about" comedy before improv riff with Conan
item.description: Brooklyn bar owner Debbie Shields won the love of the internet after a quick-witted exchange with Conan O'Brien on "Subway Takes." Shields shares her thoughts on next steps.

item.title: Gunmen kill at least 7 in attack on Jordan church, authorities say
item.description: Jordan's King Abdullah II vowed the "harshest retaliation" after gunmen carried out a deadly attack on a church.

item.title: Melania Trump secures "temporary ceasefire" in Ukrainian city
item.description: First lady Melania Trump's office says she secured a localized ceasefire for the Russian-occupied Ukrainian city of Oleshky.

item.title: Viral SubwayTakes star Debbie Shields turns quick wit into big laughs
item.description: Debbie Shields became a viral sensation on SubwayTakes with her quick wit and humor, even catching the attention of Conan O'Brien. In an interview with CBS News, she reflects on her unexpected fame and the joy she gets from making people laugh.

item.title: Unauthorized AI agents detected inside accounts at major banks
item.description: Unvetted and unauthorized third-party AI agents are operating inside the bank accounts of some U.S. customers. Axios' Madison Mills joins "CBS Mornings" to explain more.

item.title: Anthropic previews Claude Duet personal AI agent for subscribers
item.description: Anthropic said Claude Duet is only available by waitlist as a research preview for paying subscribers. Here's what it can do.

item.title: Deadly shooting in Paris suburb may be terrorist act, officials say
item.description: Officials said they are investigating a drive-by shooting in Trappes, outside Paris, as a potential terrorist act and called it a "miracle" that there weren't more casualties.

item.title: Kushner pushes back on report involving phone, spies, transfer
item.description: An excerpt from an upcoming book claims Kushner had access to alleged Middle Eastern "slush" funds when he served as a senior White House adviser during the first Trump administration. Kushner and his legal team deny the accusations.

item.title: Israel vows major West Bank operation after attack kills 2 troops
item.description: Israel's Netanyahu says he ordered the military to cordon off a major city in the occupied West Bank after an attack by Palestinian gunmen that killed two Israeli soldiers.

item.title: Meghan "deeply distressed" as dad faces child abuse material probe
item.description: Thomas Markle, the estranged father of Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, is facing a probe in the Philippines over alleged possession of child sexual abuse materials.

item.title: Why Are We All So Thirsty For Reality TV Again? | Straight Up with Kelly and Vlad
item.description: "Dancing With the Stars" is breaking voting records even after 35 seasons, cringe "Love Is Blind" clips are breaking the internet, and "Love Island" is still breaking hearts week after week. It seems we are having a reality TV renaissance. But what's behind it? Are we yearning for people to be "real" and "messy" in an online world so otherwise polished? Or are we falling for a trap? Is reality TV the furthest thing from reality of all? Vlad and Kelly are breaking it down in the very first episode of Straight Up. (Sponsored by Ketel One Vodka)

item.title: What to know about ACA open enrollment this year
item.description: As open enrollment for Affordable Care Act health insurance kicks off, consumers face rising premiums, additional identity checks, and fewer brokers.

item.title: Video shows moments leading up to police fatally shooting toddler
item.description: The Mississippi attorney general announced the police officer will not be charged in connection with the killing of 1-year-old Kohen Wiley.
